findings.reason: §10's whole value is a measurement of the fleet after the landing changes land, and the graph is what releases it, so the two new sections must join its waits.
findings.text: §10's declared waits stop at s50 while s57 and s58 are declared implementable and each changes what a landing does (s57 changes whether a commitless completion is refused, s58 changes whether a red-base merge lands), so a dispatch of §10 on the declared graph can measure a fleet that has not taken either change

findings.reason: the followup is the single instruction a coordinator acts on, and one that names five of ten open sections leaves the new work undispatched.
findings.text: the one open followup names "section 46 … section 50" and §10 only, while `plan-section-declarations` at plan.html:23 records s53, s55, s56, s57 and s58 as implementable, so a coordinator following the chain stops five sections short of the plan's own remaining work

findings.reason: a node repairing this would look for a log-completion reader that does not exist and miss that the refusal turns on a declared field the repair verb never rewrites, which decides whether the fix belongs in the arm reader or in the merge's judgement of a delivered manifest.
findings.text: s58 attributes the persistent refusal to the log's shape ("a log of that shape is not read as a completed run"), but no base reader derives an arm's completion from a log: `_baseline_suite_failure_ids` and `_head_suite_failure_ids` read the manifest's literal `completed` key (promotion_checks.py:2547, 2581), and `crew repair --arm` re-points only the revision, its own docstring stating it "says nothing about the exit status or the failure ids" (runs.py:3552-3579) — the section's own first sentence already names the real cause (neither arm *declared* `completed: true`), and a one-process log would have been refused identically

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — the tests each section names are new-file names, the s51 evidence anchor in the archive resolves (`docs/evidence/archive/delivered-work-lands-without-a-coordinator-landed.html#review-of-delivered-work-lands-without-a-coordinator-s51-4fbd87529477` is present), and the s57/s58 cross-repo commits are citations of another repository's history rather than repo-local anchors.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — s57 and s58 each name a concrete test file, two cases and a negative control that reddens at the base revision, and §57's negative control matches the base's real behaviour (the main checkout's untracked files are charged to the run through `_record_tree`'s repo fallback at promotion_release.py:1281-1297 and `_uncommitted_paths` at promotion_evidence.py:302-341).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — both sections put their gate and base-arm logs under the run directory, which survives the run, and neither names a scratch or node-local path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the two new test file names state the mechanism (`test_a_gone_worktree_is_not_charged_the_checkouts_files.py`, `test_a_multi_process_suite_arm_is_completed.py`) and neither section carries a plan label, stage name or ticket number.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — s58's stated root cause (a log of that shape "is not read as a completed run") is asserted of a reader the base does not have.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — s57 delivers one behaviour (a gone worktree reads no other tree) and s58 delivers one (a multi-process arm's completion), each with its consequence stated in the same deliverable rather than a second goal.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — `plan-section-depends-on` (plan.html:24) still declares §10's waits only through s50, so the 24-hour live-fleet measurement can be dispatched before s57 and s58 land, though both change how a landing is refused and measured.
